summary:
Lane public-repository, 2026-10-07. I wrote drafts only, below /Users/diegohaz/.claude/jobs/f65a6229/tmp/round7/decisions/public-repository. I changed no file of the worktree, made no commit, no GitHub write, and no request to production. Skills loaded: ariakit-general-workflow, ariakit-general-markdown, ariakit-general-issue-label.

(a) Findings. I read the 568 titles, and the summary and verifier texts of 59 findings. 48 findings describe a way to get around a review rule, to get a token, or to slow or stop the service (trust 17, denial 21, review-bypass 6, data-access 4). All 16 findings of the kind "security" are in the list. For 38 the weak place is in the public code, and for 10 a part of it is (I opened the code for 15, for example apps/web/src/server.ts:82-87 and packages/security/src/auth.ts:21-79). For 41 a public issue adds little: the actor has push permission, or no person can start the problem on purpose. For 7 a public issue gives a ready path: TRUST-01, AUTH-09, AUTH-16 (a session gives a GitHub token) and AUTH-07, TRUST-10, AUTH-14, TRUST-02 (a caller with no right to the data causes database work or GitHub requests). D-AUTH-01 and D-AUTH-05 already settle the fix of all 7, and each has the effort S. The list is sensitive-findings.json.

(b) Scan of apps/lab. Measured: git would add 3,897 files, 49.9 MiB (about 29.5 MiB deflated; the repository has 12.0 MB). 1,415 text files scanned: 0 GitHub tokens, 0 private keys, 0 JSON Web Tokens, 0 cloud keys. 21 secret-like values are test values of local probes. 7 e-mail addresses, all at example.com. 2,482 PNG files with no text or EXIF chunk. Real hits, path and kind only: (1) apps/lab/src/fixtures/data/people.ts:52-57, invented people of whom 3 user IDs and 4 logins are real accounts of other persons; (2) apps/lab/audit/reports/round-2/res-05/probe/results/sign-in-today.json, the avatar address of one such account; (3) apps/lab/audit/reports/gap-trust-boundary/report.md and verification.md, auth/report.md and verification.md, and content/sections/30-access-trust.html, the step path of the 7 findings (21 files name the 7 findings, 10 name the token route); (4) reports/live-authenticated.md and reports/live/report.md, production reads with times, sizes, short run IDs, and no credential; (5) section 30 line 130, a member count (10) that is not public (6 are public); (6) the local path /Users/diegohaz in 441 files, which 27 tracked files already have. No hit is a secret, a key, an e-mail address of a real person, or an internal URL.

(c) Decisions: 4 open decisions (D-PRE-41 to D-PRE-44), each with a fragment, plus 7 closed things. D-PRE-41 and D-PRE-42 depend on each other: the short form of an issue has an effect only if the branch does not publish the reports sooner. Example of the short form for TRUST-01: "apps/web/src/server.ts, lines 82 to 87, sends each /api/auth/ path to the sign-in library. Sign-in uses 4 of 30 routes. Serve these 4 and answer 404 for the others."

GitHub facts read today: the repository is public; secret scanning, push protection, and private vulnerability reporting are disabled; no SECURITY.md; 9 default labels; 20 earlier issues with no label; the active account has the admin role; gh-ariakit-bot is installed and was not run. Documentation URLs are in notes.md.

decisions.question: How much detail does a public issue give for a finding that describes a way to misuse the service?
decisions.options: full-detail (each issue has the full detail, as the 20 earlier issues; the minimal option) | short-form-for-seven (the issues and pull requests of the 7 findings name the change, the file, and the lines, and leave out the path, the chain, and the cost numbers until the fix is in production; the other 41 have the full detail) | advisory-draft (the short form, plus the detail in one private draft security advisory of ariakit/visonaut) | fix-before-issue (no issue for the 7 findings before their fix is in production)
decisions.recommended: short-form-for-seven. Reason: holding the detail costs little (7 findings, settled fixes of effort S that are first in the order), and a published issue cannot be taken back. Wrong if you judge that public code means a public weakness (then full-detail is simpler), or if a person or an agent without this computer must do the fixes (then advisory-draft).

decisions.question: What does the public branch with apps/lab hold, and when is it pushed?
decisions.options: all-at-audit-end (everything when the audit ends; the minimal option) | all-after-security-fixes (the same content, pushed after the fixes of the 7 findings and the one UPDATE of D-AUTH-05 are in production; a local branch until then) | without-audit-reports (at the audit end without the 1,030 files of apps/lab/audit/reports; section 30 and findings.json still describe the 7 findings) | lab-public-record-private (the lab on the public branch, apps/lab/audit in a new private repository)
decisions.recommended: all-after-security-fixes. Reason: the scan found no secret, so only the path of 7 findings is a reason to wait; their fixes are first; a push cannot be taken back. Cost: the lab is on one computer until the push. Wrong if a person or an agent on another computer needs the lab sooner (then all-at-audit-end with full-detail in D-PRE-41), or if you want no raw probe logs in the repository (then without-audit-reports).

decisions.question: Do the new issues get priority and difficulty labels?
decisions.options: no-labels (as the 20 earlier issues; the order is in the issue bodies; the minimal option) | priority-and-difficulty (create p0, p1, p2, easy, hard with the names, descriptions, and colors of ariakit/ariakit; the ariakit-bot identity labels each issue) | priority-only (create p0, p1, p2) | default-labels-only (bug, enhancement, documentation; no new label)
decisions.recommended: priority-and-difficulty. Reason: it is the written Ariakit rule (one priority label for each issue, a label is created only when the maintainer asks), and it helps when several agents choose work. Wrong if the order in the issue bodies is sufficient and you want no label set in this repository (then no-labels). Note: the wrapper setup allows issue edit with no question and not label create, so the creation asks for approval one time for each label.

decisions.question: Does the public repository get secret scanning with push protection and a private channel for security reports?
decisions.options: no-change (the three settings stay off, no SECURITY.md; the minimal option) | scanning-and-private-reports (turn on secret scanning, push protection, and private vulnerability reporting; no file changes) | settings-and-policy-file (the three settings and a short SECURITY.md on main)
decisions.recommended: scanning-and-private-reports. Reason: all three are disabled today (measured), they are free for a public repository (GitHub documentation), and agents will push many commits. Wrong if you expect no report from outside while the service has one consumer, or if you want no setting changed by an agent (then no-change). Small decision; the coordinator can drop it with no effect on the other three.

closed: C1. Who files the issues. Closed by: "You can file the issues yourself." and "I authorize the implementation, the GitHub writes, ...". The implementation files with the active GitHub account (the bot identity is only for labels), uses instruction titles with no prefix as the 20 earlier issues, searches open issues first (0 open issues today, 1 open pull request #253), reads each body back after the write, and puts no token or session value into an issue. Record: section 15, list your-answers-word, item 11 goes away.

C2. Fewer issues with a topological order. Closed by: "I just think we should group findings into fewer issues that make sense together and have a topological order for issues so we can work on some in parallel while others wait." This is a task of the issue plan. Facts from this lane for the plan: the fixes of TRUST-01, AUTH-09, AUTH-16, AUTH-07, TRUST-10, AUTH-14, and TRUST-02 come first (D-AUTH-01, D-AUTH-05, effort S each), the one UPDATE of D-AUTH-05 is in that first group, and the public text for OPS-01 and STATE-03 must not name TRUST-02 as the way to cause a failed GitHub read before TRUST-02 is fixed.

C3. The lab goes to a branch, not to main. Closed by: "Yes, I think we should put it in a branch when we're done with the audit." Closed: the place and the earliest time. Open: the content and if the push waits for the first fixes (D-PRE-42). Record: section 70 and the fragment code-lab-branch.

C4. The invented people of the lab. No word of the maintainer is necessary; "I authorize the implementation" covers a correction. Before the push, apps/lab/src/fixtures/data/people.ts:52-57 gets logins and user IDs of no real account (check with gh api users/LOGIN and gh api user/ID, each must answer 404) and one sentence that says that the people are invented. Raw probe results are not edited by hand.

C5. No secret in the files, so no secret to change. Closed by a measurement: 1,415 text files, 0 tokens, 0 keys; the 21 secret-like values are test values (20 are hyphenated words, 1 is 0123456789abcdef three times); no PNG has a text or EXIF chunk.

C6. The local path /Users/diegohaz (1,690 times in 441 files). Closed by a measurement: 27 tracked files of the public repository have the same path today. No action. A script can replace it if the maintainer asks; this lane does not recommend it.

C7. A reminder for the day of the first other customer (standing rule 5). The judgment of this lane holds while only the members of one organization can sign in. Before a second customer, a person reads sensitive-findings.json and the part access-who of section 30 again. It belongs beside item 10 of the list your-answers-word.
wrongInRecord: TRUST-01, summary in content/findings.json: it says "each sign-in of any GitHub account stores user, account, session, and audit rows". The verification of the record corrected this (the sign-in App is private, so only organization members can sign in). Section 30 has the correction; the summary keeps the wide claim.

TRUST-02, summary in content/findings.json: it says "one outside account can use up the App rate budget". The same correction applies: the actor is an organization member without push permission, or a person who lost access and kept a session.

AUTH-16, title in content/findings.json: "GitHub OAuth user tokens are stored and never read". The verification of the record found that a route of the sign-in library returns them. "Never read" is true only for the code of the repository.

List your-answers-word, item 11 (r7): it says that the implementation, the package publication, and the change in ariakit/ariakit each need a separate authorization. The words of 2026-10-07 give these. The report to Ariakit UI of the two tested rewrites is not in those words and stays.
List your-answers-word, item 4 (r7): it says that the two writes to production D1 run only on a separate instruction. The words of 2026-10-07 authorize "the two writes to production D1".

Section 30, line 130: "the organization has 10 members". Correct for the account of a member (measured: 10). The public count is 6 (measured), so the record gives a count that is not public. It names no member.

New fact that the record does not have: 3 GitHub user IDs and 4 logins of the 6 invented lab people (apps/lab/src/fixtures/data/people.ts:52-57) are real accounts of other persons (public GitHub API).
No wrong line number: each of the 15 code places of the record that I opened is correct in the worktree today.
doubts: No attack was tested. Each judgment of what a public issue adds is a reading of the record and of the code. I opened the code for 15 of the 48 findings and used the record for the other 33.
"About 2 issues" for the 7 findings is an assumption: the issue groups are not made yet. More issues make the short form of D-PRE-41 cost more.
D-PRE-41 and D-PRE-42 depend on each other. "Short form" together with "everything, when the audit ends" gives no gain. The record has no way to couple two decisions; the two panels say it in words.
The time to the deploy of the first fixes is not estimated. The contract goes first in its own pull requests, and D-AUTH-05 removes the object of the contract words about encrypted tokens.
The recommended option of D-PRE-42 keeps the lab on one computer until the push. If UI work must start on another computer in the same days as the first fixes, the recommendation is wrong.

The scan is a pattern scan and can miss a secret of an unknown form. I opened 1 of the 2,482 pictures and did not decode the 1 inline picture of section 65. I did not trace each of the 52 UUID values to its source.
The file list is of 2026-10-07, about 17:05, while revision r8 was in work (apps/lab/public/cards changed at 17:01). The counts can move by some files.
29.5 MiB is the sum of each file after deflate; git can store less with deltas.
The bot wrapper gh-ariakit-bot is installed and was not run. Not known: if its token lookup works, and if the bot account may create a label in ariakit/visonaut.
Nobody tested push protection against the probe files. Their test values with a token prefix have 16 or 17 characters, so a match is not probable.
D-PRE-44 is near the question of the task and not in it. The coordinator can drop it.
The priorities in the example of D-PRE-43 are an assumption of this lane.
TRUST-06 (an OIDC token is accepted again) has no fix in a settled list. The issue plan must keep it or drop it with a reason.
I read the GitHub documentation through a tool that gives a summary and quotes. The quotes are as the tool gave them; nobody opened the pages in a browser.

The decision contexts have 151 to 209 words. AUTHORING.md asks for one or two sentences; the task asked for an explanation with an example. The coordinator can move detail from a context into its fragment.
